title: Florida House, District 77
what_it_does: Represents District 77 (Part of Lee) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings. Positions have not been researched yet.

candidates.name: Tiffany Esposito
candidates.occupation: President and CEO of SWFL Inc. (regional chamber of commerce); state representative since 2022
candidates.background: Tiffany Esposito was born and raised in Lee County and earned a bachelor's degree in communication and an MBA from Florida Gulf Coast University. She is president and CEO of SWFL Inc., a regional chamber of commerce, and has served in the Florida House since November 2022. She chairs the Lee County legislative delegation and lives in San Carlos Park.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

taxes.summary: Her campaign site says she will work to cut taxes and remove regulations so businesses can reinvest, and describes fighting for lower taxes and a fiscally responsible budget.
taxes.quote: In Tallahassee she will work to remove burdensome regulations and cut taxes so local businesses can reinvest in high paying jobs for our residents.

sources.title: Issues - Tiffany Esposito for Florida House
Meet Tiffany - Tiffany Esposito for Florida House

property_tax.summary: Voted yes on HJR 1-F (June 2, 2026), which put a $250,000 non-school homestead exemption on the November ballot, and yes on HJR 203 (Feb. 19, 2026) to phase out non-school homestead taxes; local coverage noted the whole Lee delegation voted for HJR 203.

immigration.summary: Voted yes on SB 2-C (Feb. 13, 2025), which created a State Board of Immigration Enforcement, funded state cooperation with federal immigration enforcement and added criminal penalties tied to immigration status.

abortion.summary: Voted yes on SB 300 (April 13, 2023), the six-week abortion limit. Her campaign site says she is a defender of life at all stages beginning at conception.
abortion.quote: Tiffany is a staunch defender of life at all stages, beginning at conception.

sources.title: Florida House roll call, SB 300 (Heartbeat Protection Act, six-week abortion limit) passage (Yeas 70, Nays 40)

guns.summary: Voted yes on HB 543 (March 24, 2023), which allowed permitless concealed carry. Her site says the right to keep and bear arms is not conditional.
guns.quote: As a gun owner and concealed weapons permit holder, she does not believe these rights are conditional and will always protect our ability to defend ourselves.

education_choice.summary: Voted yes on HB 1 (2023), which made every K-12 student eligible for a state scholarship usable at private schools or for home education, on March 17, 2023.

housing.summary: Her site says housing costs are pricing families out and that she is dedicated to finding solutions so workforce and fixed-income families can buy homes; it does not name specific programs.
housing.quote: She is dedicated to finding solutions that provide our workforce and fixed income families the opportunity to achieve the American dream of home ownership.

environment.summary: Her site calls water quality the cornerstone of Southwest Florida's way of life and commits to completing projects that address Lake Okeechobee discharges, while also backing infrastructure for growth.
environment.quote: Tiffany is committed to ensuring the completion of projects that will provide permanent solutions to harmful levels of Lake Okeechobee discharges.

crime.summary: Her site says she supports law enforcement, paramedics and firefighters and will work to ensure they have the tools and resources to keep the community safe.
crime.quote: Tiffany supports our law enforcement officers, paramedics, and fire fighters and will always work to ensure they have the tools and resources necessary to keep our community safe.

candidates.name: Cornelius Fowler
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Farmworker and truck driver; vice president of IAM Local Lodge 2152
candidates.background: Cornelius Fowler grew up in the Glades farming region, graduated from Glades Central High School and attended Palm Beach State College. He works as a farmworker and truck driver and is vice president of International Association of Machinists Local Lodge 2152 and of the union's Florida state council. He ran for the same seat in 2024 and lives in the Lehigh Acres area.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

abortion.summary: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey he listed the right of every citizen to make decisions about the health of their own bodies as a policy passion; he did not address the six-week law directly.
abortion.quote: The rights For every citizen to be able to make their own decisions or the health of their own bodies.

sources.title: Cornelius Fowler - Ballotpedia (2024 Candidate Connection survey)

other_issues.title: Public schools and labor
other_issues.summary: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey he said he wants public schools well funded, supports workers' right to organize, and would first file a bill for paid early education and high-school trade certificates. He named health care, homeowner insurance, affordable housing and education as the state's biggest challenges.
